title: Stamping the Grid
description:
You are given an `m x n` binary matrix `grid` where `0` represents an empty cell and `1` represents an occupied cell. You also have an unlimited supply of rectangular stamps of fixed dimensions `stampHeight x stampWidth`.

You want to place stamps on the grid subject to these rules:
- Every empty (`0`) cell must be covered by at least one stamp.
- No occupied (`1`) cell may be covered by any stamp.
- Stamps may overlap each other, may not be rotated, and must lie completely inside the grid.

Return `true` if it is possible to cover all empty cells, or `false` otherwise.
hints: Build a 2D prefix sum over grid so you can test in O(1) whether any stampHeight x stampWidth rectangle contains zero occupied cells.
Whenever a stamp fits at top-left (r, c), greedily record it in a 2D difference array; after computing the 2D prefix sum of the difference array, verify every 0-cell has coverage > 0.

examples.explanation: Two overlapping 4x3 stamps cover the entire 5x3 region of empty cells without touching any occupied 1-cell.
No 2x2 stamp can fit anywhere in the grid without overlapping an occupied cell, leaving empty cells uncovered.
Every cell is already occupied (no empty cells exist), so the condition holds vacuously.
